support__workflows__emergency_exception_workflow.md:62:- **Reasoning**:  Not executing a planned disaster recovery failover exercise will create immediate compliance problems for a customer's business and may even result in fines. If timelines are very short, this qualifies for an emergency. Otherwise, with customer agreement this situation may be treated as a normal support ticket with priority set to 'high' as it is still important to restore the secondary site quickly for business continuity purposes.

64:#### Take a break

66-Consider taking breaks during emergency calls. Taking a break can help you to feel more refreshed while ensuring our customers get the best help we can provide.
67-
68:At the beginning of the call, set expectations with the customer by letting them know you plan to take a break each 90 minutes (or so), if the call goes that long.
69-
70-When the call begins, set a timer to count down and notify you that it's time for a break. (If you forget, observe the call duration in Zoom.)
71-
72-When the timer goes off, summarize the current state, make sure everyone knows when the call will resume and how to join. If your timer expires but you're not at a reasonable stopping point, extend the timer by a small amount.
73-
74-During the break:
75-
76-- Stop actively working on the emergency
--
242:  During an emergency [taking a break](#take-a-break), can be very beneficial for results for our customers as it permits the incoming CEOC to get up to speed. The outgoing and incoming CEOC benefit from discussing ideas in a low pressure environment.
243-  - Advise the customer that the call will be paused, and agree on a time to reconvene.
244-  - During the 30 minute break, discuss with the incoming CEOC:
245-    - What is the problem the customer is facing?
246-    - What activities have been performed?
247-    - What issues or theories have been ruled out?
248-    - What is the current theory of the source of the issue?
249-    - What alternative options have not been considered?
250-    - Does this emergency require an escalation?
